reden: Yes. The audit explicitly reports: “authorizedSigner may be address(0), letting any invalid signature authorize settle()/close()”. It identifies the same root cause (openChannel allows authorizedSigner = address(0); ecrecover/_recoverSigner can return address(0) for invalid signatures), the same affected functions (openChannel, settle, close), the same exploit path (any garbage/invalid signature passes when authorizedSigner == 0), and the same fix (reject zero authorizedSigner and/or zero recovered signer). Fixing what the audit notes would fix the described vulnerability.
